chapter: Faith, Paris life and later years
title: American musicians abroad and the Algerian war's effect on Paris
summary: Clarke says the colons who came to France after the Algerian war brought colonial racism, which police and law limited.

blocks.x: Well, listen, one other thing I just wanted to ask you was about the guys that have come and lived abroad, you know, the different guys we know like Ben Webster and --
-- and I knew Stuff, too. Stuff lived over here a long time, didn't he?
Yeah, well so did Ben, didn't he?
And Don Byas. And who else? Who are the guys that -- I mean is there like a -- is there like a small American colony or --
See, but since the war, the Algerian war, --

Because the colones came to the mother-land which they had never seen before, with the same attitude they had in the colonies, which were ordering people around and segregation and hate, and -- they came here with that.
And infected the Garden of Eden.
That's right. Exactly. That's exactly what happened.
I never did realize that. And changed.
Oh, changed the whole thing, because the government gave them money for everything they'd lost there, so they came here and they bought businesses. They even bought
places they wouldn't even allow colored people in. And France has never been a country like that. But the police broke that up right away, because that's in the Napoleonic law, you know.
Because whoever seeks freedom from oppression --
-- France has its arms open. Napoleon said that.
So it broke that up right quick. But the colones are trying to get back in another way.
Yeah. They've just ruined France. Well, they came in from Algiers.
Where they were kicking Arabs around.
Morocco, Tunis, and in black Africa.
Where they were kicking people around.
After these people gained their freedom. Well, then the colones left and came to the mainland.
By true French people who lived here.
But these people, they're not French. See, they were Italians --
